subject: Hospitality
title: Drive-Throughs and Speed
description: A quick, practical guide to Drive-Throughs and Speed.

hook.text: About 70% of McDonald's revenue in the U.S. comes through the drive-through window. The dining room is almost secondary.

buildup.text: Drive-throughs appeared in the 1940s and exploded with car culture. Speed became the ultimate competitive advantage.

discovery.text: Chains measure 'speed of service' obsessively. A Wendy's target is under 3 minutes from order to window pickup.

twist.text: AI is replacing human order-takers. Some drive-throughs now use voice AI that upsells based on time of day and weather.

climax.text: The drive-through reshaped American cities. Restaurants, banks, and pharmacies all adopted the format because cars dominate.

punchline.text: 70% of sales from a window. America eats from behind a steering wheel.

quiz.question: Approximately what percentage of McDonald's U.S. revenue comes from the drive-through?
